source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A relatively preserved ejection fraction, with heart failure symptoms resulting primarily from impaired ventricular relaxation and filling (diastolic dysfunction)","B":"Sharing essentially the same underlying pathophysiology as HFrEF, with fairly little meaningful distinction between the two conditions clinically","C":"A condition that essentially never produces any noticeable symptoms in the clients who happen to have this diagnosis","D":"A significantly reduced ejection fraction reflecting impaired systolic contraction, the hallmark feature of HFrEF rather than HFpEF"}}
source_row.rationale: HFpEF is characterized by a relatively preserved ejection fraction, with heart failure symptoms resulting primarily from impaired ventricular relaxation and filling (diastolic dysfunction), distinct from HFrEF, which involves significantly reduced ejection fraction from impaired systolic contraction.
